findings.note: McNeely is listed among the sponsors of House Bill 1231, No Voter Registration Changes At DMV (primary sponsors are three other members). The bill would stop voters from changing an existing registration (address, name, party) at the DMV website or DMV offices and require those changes at county boards of elections. The bill text keeps the DMV question asking applicants whether they are U.S. citizens. Referred to the House Rules committee on 5/12/2026.
subjects: citizenship question on DMV registration form

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (House passed 66-47)
findings.note: Member's vote page lists an Aye on second reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text (see the bill page) covers photo-ID cure deadlines for provisional ballots, a photocopy of ID with military and overseas ballots, a citizenship question at driver-license offices and on voter registration applications, and sharing of driver-license data with the State Board of Elections. The same vote page also shows an Aye on an amendment (A1 Blackwell, 112-0) and a No on amendment A3 Dahle (47-66, failed).
subjects: photo ID with military and overseas ballots

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, motion to concur with Senate changes (passed 62-47)
findings.note: Member's vote page lists an Aye on the House vote to concur in the Senate version of HB 958. The bill page says it was ratified 2026-08-06 and vetoed by the Governor 2026-08-17; the page does not say whether the veto was overridden.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes: veto by the Governor (context for the votes above)
findings.note: Bill page shows primary sponsors Blackwell and Stevens (McNeely is not listed), ratified 2026-08-06, vetoed 2026-08-17, placed on the calendar for 2026-09-02. Saved only as context for the two votes above.
